notes.characters: Bandit has an appealing mask, rounded silhouette and expressive face in mobile/r11-hop.png and mobile/r13-results.png; the striped tails, banded hatchlings and sleeping gators distinguish several roles in desktop/r05-whippers.png and desktop/r08-barn.png. Repeated identical silhouettes and the modest silhouette difference between ordinary and scarred swimmers keep the cast at the 7 anchor rather than premium polish.
notes.environment: The lush painted banks, rocks and spring in desktop/r01-title.png promise a richer world than the repeated straight texture strips and sparse isolated props in desktop/r04-pond.png and desktop/r07-feeding.png. Mobile/r08-barn.png changes the floor material but provides little enclosing architecture, leaving gameplay closer to coherent flat assembly than the consistent painted scene required for 7.
notes.depth: Painted character shading and waterline ripples provide local volume in mobile/r03-l1-start.png, but long hard oval shadows and ruler-straight banks flatten desktop/r11-hop.png. Desktop/r08-barn.png and desktop/r09-night.png establish warm and cool moods, yet lamps, beams and translucent rectangular water patches read as separate overlays rather than integrated scene lighting.
notes.readability: Large open jaws and yellow warning badges are easy to spot in mobile/r03-l1-start.png and mobile/r11-hop.png. However, the exact safe riding area is not visually separated from the head, hatchlings blend into busy grass in mobile/r06-nursery.png, and dark scenery plus overlapping alerts in desktop/r12-endless.png prevent consistently immediate phone-scale interpretation.
notes.ui: Mobile/r13-results.png and mobile/r15-intro.png have strong panel hierarchy, clear actions and legible goal information, while desktop/r02-map.png offers orderly level grouping. The text-heavy mobile/r14-help.png, jagged outlined headings and abstract unlabeled ring meter in mobile/r03-l1-start.png hold the otherwise designed UI at 7.
notes.juice: Mobile/r11-hop.png and desktop/r11-hop.png visibly show a lifted pose, carried snacks, motion strokes and takeoff puffs; mobile/r06-nursery.png adds a pickup sparkle. These establish feedback, but simple white primitives, repeated placid swimmer poses and thin wakes in desktop/r04-pond.png fall short of the rubric's 6.5 gate; stills do not establish animation timing or responsiveness.
notes.mobile: Mobile/r01-title.png and mobile/r13-results.png reflow cleanly with generous visible buttons, and mobile/r03-l1-start.png preserves a useful northward view. Mobile/r10-boss.png crops most of the signature boss, mobile/r07-feeding.png places the Lure button over an active hazard area, and mobile/r14-help.png requires scrolling through a dense manual, so portrait framing is not consistently shippable at the 7 anchor.
notes.authenticity: The Hot Springs wording and non-affiliation statement in mobile/r01-title.png, plus farm facts in desktop/r13-results.png, give explicit regional context without suggesting endorsement. The actual playfields in desktop/r07-feeding.png and mobile/r08-barn.png still resemble generic cartoon pools with scattered husbandry props; little visible architecture makes Hot Springs recognizable independently of text.
notes.ip_gate: PASS on the supplied captures: no recognizable commercial-game mascot, birds/pigs/slingshots motif, real logo or real-world signage is visible in desktop/r01-title.png, mobile/r13-results.png or the gameplay captures. The real attraction is named in explanatory title copy with an explicit non-affiliation statement in mobile/r01-title.png; no severity-5 characters gap is triggered.

gaps.issue: The gator's safe back and dangerous snout share one uninterrupted shaded silhouette; the detached warning triangle and thin red ellipse do not clearly delimit the rideable area.
gaps.fix: Paint a quieter broad saddle plane across the back and render a translucent tooth-shaped danger wedge over the actual snout footprint, with a short visual tether from the warning badge.

gaps.issue: Full-width repeated grass, sand and water strips produce a striped board with sparse pasted props, far below the rich setting shown on the title.
gaps.fix: Commission matching bank-edge tiles with irregular grass tufts, stone coping corners and shallow-water transitions; compose several seeded variants along lane boundaries while keeping traversal centers clear.

gaps.issue: Only the boss's head and a small body fragment enter the portrait capture, losing the massive silhouette that distinguishes the desktop encounter.
gaps.fix: Use a portrait-specific boss staging position or temporary camera zoom that shows its head and substantial torso together; add an edge warning silhouette before its entrance.

gaps.issue: Land gators cast long, hard oval shadows displaced to one side, while Bandit's compact shadow follows a different treatment; some animals appear to float above the floor.
gaps.fix: Render a tight dark contact shadow under each belly and feet plus a softer low-opacity cast shadow using a radial-gradient mask, with one shared light direction and height-dependent offset.

gaps.issue: Visible translucent blue rectangles beneath swimmers and sharp-edged flashlight polygons expose the lighting construction; eyeshine sits as a glowing forehead spot rather than convincing eye reflection.
gaps.fix: Clip water tint to each submerged silhouette, feather beam sides with gradient masks, and place small reflected highlights inside the painted pupils using per-sprite eye anchors.

gaps.issue: The barn reads as yellow straw strips beside outdoor-looking water; heat lamps hang from thin horizontal lines without enough visible structure to establish an interior.
gaps.fix: Paint overhead timber supports, peripheral stalls and trough sidewalls in the same perspective; draw chains from visible rafters and pool warm light beneath each lamp with subtle cool ambient fill.

gaps.issue: Small green hatchlings disappear into the equally busy yellow-green grass texture, making the supposedly traversable banks difficult to scan.
gaps.fix: Reduce grass texture contrast in occupied lanes and add a dark silhouette rim plus a restrained warm belly highlight to hatchlings; retain the red mouth band as a secondary cue.

gaps.issue: The large Lure control covers active lower-right board space during feeding, and warning badges near the right edge are cropped in the hop capture.
gaps.fix: Reserve a persistent bottom control gutter outside the world viewport and clamp alert badges inside portrait safe bounds, connecting them to offscreen hazard positions with small directional pointers.

gaps.issue: Hop feedback consists of plain vertical strokes and overlapping white circles, pickup rays are similarly geometric, and swimmers mostly retain a placid repeated pose.
gaps.fix: Commission curved painted dust and splash sprites, taper motion streaks along the hop arc, and add separate paddle, anticipatory jaw and bite poses with brighter local splash accents.

gaps.issue: Help is a dense scrolling text manual, the ring meter looks like anonymous capsules, and outlined headings have visibly stair-stepped edges alongside otherwise smooth controls.
gaps.fix: Replace role paragraphs with illustrated gator cards and short captions, use recognizable striped-tail ring icons, and render heading outlines with high-resolution strokeText before downsampling.

gaps.issue: Hot Springs identity depends largely on title copy and fact cards; gameplay lacks a distinctive regional farm layout or visitor-facing enclosure language.
gaps.fix: Commission original Ozark stonework, fenced visitor paths, husbandry gates and a distant wooded ridge, using fictional enclosure labels and no real logos; carry the title's spring-rock motif into selected playable banks.
